holidays.name: National Rubber Duckie Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the squeaky yellow bath companion that has watched over bubble baths for generations. Fans line up their ducks, give them a splash, and maybe let them race in the tub.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that grew out of the rubber duck's long popularity. Rubber ducks became bath toys in the late 19th century, and Sesame Street's Ernie helped make them iconic with the 1970 song 'Rubber Duckie'.
holidays.funFact: In 1992, a shipping container carrying about 28,800 plastic bath toys fell into the Pacific Ocean. The toys drifted for years and helped oceanographers study ocean currents.

holidays.name: National Peach Melba Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy the classic dessert of poached peaches, vanilla ice cream, and raspberry sauce. It is a fancy treat with a very elegant backstory.
holidays.origin: Famed French chef Auguste Escoffier created the dessert around 1892 at the Savoy Hotel in London to honor Australian soprano Nellie Melba. It was originally served on an ice sculpture of a swan.
holidays.funFact: Nellie Melba also inspired Melba toast, which was named after her because she ate it while ill in 1897.

holidays.name: Stuffed Mushroom Day
holidays.description: A day for savory mushroom caps loaded with cheese, herbs, breadcrumbs, or sausage. It is a party-appetizer favorite that gets its own spotlight.
holidays.origin: This is a food-lover's observance with no single official founder. Stuffed mushrooms became a popular appetizer in mid-20th-century American entertaining.
holidays.funFact: Mushrooms are more closely related to animals than to plants, so a stuffed mushroom is technically a distant relative of your dinner guests.

holidays.name: Make Your Dreams Come True Day
holidays.description: A motivational observance that encourages people to stop procrastinating and take real steps toward their biggest goals. It falls just as many New Year's resolutions start to wobble.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial self-improvement day. Its timing in mid-January is likely meant to give resolutions a boost when motivation tends to fade.
holidays.funFact: Research often cited in the media suggests many people abandon their resolutions by mid-January, so this day is perfectly timed as a pep talk.

holidays.name: Korean American Day
holidays.description: A day recognizing the contributions of Korean Americans to the United States, honoring their history, culture, and communities.
holidays.origin: It marks the arrival of the first Korean immigrants to Hawaii on January 13, 1903, who came aboard the SS Gaelic to work on sugar plantations. The day has been officially recognized by the U.S. Congress and many states.
holidays.funFact: The first group of 102 Korean immigrants who landed in Honolulu in 1903 kicked off a wave of migration that now includes more than two million Korean Americans.
